newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian inflation slows to 17.1 pct in August.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian inflation slows to 17.1 pct in August.

text.p: Bulgaria's monthly consumer price inflation slowed to 17.1 percent in August from 23.3 percent in July, National Statistics Institute figures show.
BULGARIAN CONSUMER PRICES AUGUST JULY AUGUST'95

Inflation for the first eight months already tops the annual inflation target of 104 percent for 1996 in the central government budget, which was revised in July to accomodate the cost of structural reform.
Food prices rose by 21.5 percent, non-foods rose 12.8 percent and services gained 14.9 percent in August.
"Inflation eased in August but it was far from the one-digit expectations due to rises of energy and fuel prices and the wheat shortage," a NSI official who declined to be named told Reuters.
An acute wheat shortfall caused flour and bread prices rising some 50 percent in August.
The government decided in July that energy prices should be revised monthly in line with the lev/dollar exchange rate to meet funding requirements of multilateral lenders.
Electricity and fuel prices rose 22 percent in August alone and surged 226.5 percent for the first eight months, the NSI said.
Prices of transportation and communication services rose 156 percent from January through August while food prices advanced by 109.5 percent during the same period, figures showed.
The lev has lost some 230 percent of its value since the beginning of the year, when it traded near 71 to the dollar. It slumped to around 237 per dollar last week on the domestic interbank market.
Local economists said they expected annual inflation near to 150 percent. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
